Rashi on Pesachim 92a:10:1.hebrew: הא דאמרן - דחזי לאורתא, ומשום גזירה דשנה הבאה דחיוה ב"ה:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:10:1.english: As we have said - For he is fit for the evening, and because of a decree [concerning] the following year, Beit Hillel deferred him.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:11:1.hebrew: ואינה דוחה שבת - בפ' אלו דברים, ולא עביד פסח, ושבות דרבנן הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:11:1.english: And it does not override Shabbat - In the chapter [entitled] Eilu Devarim, and [thus] he does not offer the Paschal lamb, and it is a rabbinic prohibition.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:12:1.english: We may not bring it - [The] scalpel for circumcision.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:12:2.hebrew: דרך חצרות - אף על גב דרשויות דרבנן נינהו, וידחה פסחו — שאם יש לו זכר למול מעכבו, דתניא: "מילת זכריו ועבדיו מעכבין את הפסח" — וליכא למימר משום כרת ד"ערל זכר אשר לא ימול וגו'", דמילה דדחיא שבת בזמנה, וקטן לאו בר כרת הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:12:2.english: Through courtyards - Even though [carrying through these] domains is [only] a rabbinic [prohibition], and [by not bringing the scalpel] his Paschal offering will be deferred — for if he has a male to circumcise, it prevents him [from offering it], as it was taught [in a baraita]: "The circumcision of his males and his slaves prevents [him from offering] the Paschal lamb" — still, one cannot say [that he should carry it] because of the karet of "an uncircumcised male who is not circumcised, etc.," for [a] circumcision that overrides Shabbat [is only one performed] in its [proper] time, and a minor is not subject to karet.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:13:1.hebrew: אונן - אנינות לילה מדרבנן, דאמרן לעיל אוכל פסחו לערב:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:13:1.english: An acute mourner - Acute mourning at night is by rabbinic decree, as we said above: "he eats his Paschal offering in the evening."

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:14:1.hebrew: מצורע - שטבל והעריב שמשו בשביעי, נכנס בשמיני למחנה לויה לשער נקנור, שלא נתקדש בקדושת עזרה, כדכתיב בקרא (ויקרא י״ד:י״א): "והעמיד הכהן המטהר את האיש המיטהר ואותם לפני ה' וגו'". ובעזרה עצמה לא היה נכנס, אלא מכניס ידיו לבוהנות, לפי שאין מחוסר כפורים נכנס לה, כדאמרי' [במכות] (דף ח:): "טמא יהיה" — לרבות טבול יום, "עוד טומאתו בו" — לרבות מחוסר כפורים, שאם נכנסו למקדש חייבין כרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:14:1.english: A leper - who immersed and whose sun set on the seventh [day] enters on the eighth [day] into the Levite camp, to the Gate of Nikanor, which was not consecrated with the sanctity of the Temple Courtyard, as it is written in the verse (Leviticus 14:11): "And the priest who purifies shall stand the man being purified and them before the Lord, etc." And into the Courtyard itself he would not enter; rather, he inserts his hands for [the application to] his thumbs, because one who lacks atonement may not enter it, as we say [in Makkot] (8b): "[He] shall be impure" — to include one who immersed that day; "his impurity is still upon him" — to include one who lacks atonement, that if they enter the Temple they are liable to excision.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:14:2.hebrew: וראה קרי בו ביום - ונדחה ממחנה לויה, כדאמרי' באלו דברים (דף סז:) דבעל קרי משתלח חוץ לשתי מחנות. וטובל לקרוייו, דלצרעתו טבל מאתמול. אף על פי שטבול יום אחר דקרי אינו נכנס, דכתיב (דברים כ״ג:י״ב) "כי יהיה בך איש וגו' וכבא השמש יבא אל תוך המחנה" — זה נכנס להר הבית להכניס ידיו לבוהנות, כדי שיאכל פסחו לערב:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:14:2.english: And he saw an occurrence [of semen] on that day - and he is excluded from the Camp of the Levites, as we say in [the chapter] Eilu Devarim (67b), that one who has experienced a seminal emission is sent outside of two camps. And he immerses for his seminal emission, for regarding his leprosy he [already] immersed yesterday. Even though another tevul yom from a seminal emission may not enter [the Temple Mount], as it is written (Deuteronomy 23:12): "If there be among you any man, etc., and when the sun goes down, he shall come into the camp" — this one enters the Temple Mount to insert his hands for [the application to] the thumbs [and toes], so that he may eat his Paschal offering in the evening.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:15:1.hebrew: יבא עשה - דפסח שיש בו כרת, וידחה עשה דטבול יום בהר הבית, שאין בו כרת אלא בעזרה. ואי משום דמכניס ידיו לעזרה, הא אמרינן בשחיטת קדשים בפ"ג (דף לב:), איכא למ"ד ביאה במקצת לאו שמה ביאה, ואיכא למאן דאמר: הואיל והותרה לו אותה ביאה מקצת לצרעתו — אע"פ שענוש כרת משום מחוסר כפורים והתירו הכתוב, דכתיב "לפני ה'" — הותרה לו אף לקרוייו:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:15:1.english: A positive commandment will come - [that] of the Paschal offering, which carries [the penalty of] karet, and override the positive commandment regarding a tevul yom on the Temple Mount, which does not carry karet — [as karet applies] only in the Courtyard. And if [you are concerned] because he brings his hands into the Courtyard, we have stated in Shechitat Kodashim [Zevachim], in the third chapter (32b): there is one [authority] who says that partial entry is not considered entry, and there is one who says [that] since that partial entry was permitted to him for his tzara'at — even though he is liable to karet as one lacking atonement, and Scripture permitted it to him, as it is written, "before the Lord" — it was also permitted to him for his seminal emission.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:16:1.hebrew: וא"ר יוחנן - עשה שאין בו כרת דקאמר תנא דברייתא, לאו דוקא, דאפילו עשה אין בו בטבול יום במחנה לויה, אלא דרבנן הוא; וקרא דכבא השמש, במחנה שכינה קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:16:1.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said - [The] positive commandment that has no karet which the Tanna of the baraita stated is not exact, for there is not even a positive commandment regarding a tevul yom [entering] the Levite camp; rather, it is rabbinic. And the verse "when the sun sets" is speaking of the camp of the Shechinah.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:16:2.hebrew: חצר החדשה - הר הבית, וקרי לה חדשה מפני חידוש שחידשו והוסיפו על קדושתו בו ביום, ואמרו: טבול יום לא יכנס לה. והכי גמיר ר' יוחנן מרביה, דדבר זה חידוש. וגבי פסח לא העמידו דבריהם לאיסור (דמצורע) [דבעל קרי] מלבוא, אלא התירוהו ליכנס ולטהר, שלא ידחה מפסח:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:16:2.english: The new courtyard - [This is] the Temple Mount, and [Scripture] calls it "new" because of an innovation that they innovated and added to its sanctity on that day, and they said: One who has immersed on that day may not enter it. And so Rabbi Yoḥanan learned as a tradition from his teacher, that this matter is an innovation. And regarding the Paschal offering, they did not uphold their words regarding the prohibition of one who had a seminal emission from entering; rather, they permitted him to enter and to become pure, so that he would not be pushed off from [bringing] the Paschal offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:1:1.hebrew: וכן מי שליקטו לו עצמות - אביו ואמו, אמרי' במועד קטן (דף ח.), מתאבל עליהן כל היום כולו, ולערב אין מתאבל עליהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:1:1.english: And similarly, one for whom bones were gathered - [the bones of] his father and his mother; we say in Moed Katan (8a) [that] he mourns for them the entire day, and in the evening he does not mourn for them.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:1:2.hebrew: טובל ואוכל בקדשים - לערב, דאפילו יום גופיה מדרבנן הוא; הלכך, בלילה ליכא אנינות:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:1:2.english: He immerses and eats consecrated [foods] - In the evening, for even the day itself is [only] by rabbinic decree; therefore, at night there is no acute mourning.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:2:1.english: Like one who separates from the grave - And he requires sprinkling [on the] third and seventh [days].

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:3:1.hebrew: לא העמידו דבריהם - לאוסרו באכילת פסחו מפני אנינות דדבריהם, דהא פסח כרת הוא. אבל אכילת קדשים עשה בעלמא הוא — "ואכלו אותם אשר כפר בהם" (שמות כ״ט:ל״ג):
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:3:1.english: They did not uphold their statement - [That is,] to forbid him from eating his Paschal lamb because of rabbinic acute mourning, for [neglecting] the Paschal lamb [carries] karet. However, eating sacrificial food is merely a positive commandment — [as it is written:] "And they shall eat those [things] with which atonement was made" (Exodus 29:33).

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:4:1.english: One who gathers - [This] implies [that] he himself gathered them.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:5:1.hebrew: מחלוקת בערל נכרי - שאינו מקבל טומאה בנכריותו, דב"ה סברי: גזירה שמא יטמא במת לשנה הבאה עה"פ, ויאמר: אשתקד לא טהרתי מכל טומא' עד יום ע"פ שנתגיירתי וטבלתי ואכלתי, והשתא נמי אטבול ואיכול; ולא ידע דאשתקד נכרי הוה ולא קיבל טומאה בנכריותו, אבל עכשיו הוא טמא. הלכך, כשמתגייר ממתין שבעה, שאין לך טומאה שעברה עליו שלא טהר ממנה. ואע"ג דמשום זיבה בעי שמנה משום כפרה, כיון דאי אפשר דלייתי כפרה — דהא לא קבל טומאה בנכריותו — אי אמרת נגזר, לא מייתי לעולם פסח, וכולי האי לא גזרו:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:5:1.english: The dispute is about an uncircumcised gentile - who does not contract ritual impurity in his gentile state; for Beit Hillel hold [that there is a] rabbinic decree lest he become impure through a corpse the following year on Passover eve, and say, "Last year I was not purified from any impurity until the day of Passover eve when I converted, immersed, and ate [the Paschal offering], so now too I will immerse and eat," not realizing that last year he was a gentile and did not contract impurity in his gentile state, whereas now he is impure. Therefore, when he converts, he waits seven [days], for there is no impurity that passed over him from which he has not become pure. And even though on account of zivah [flux impurity] one requires an eighth [day] for an atonement [offering], since it is impossible for him to bring an atonement [offering] — for he did not contract impurity in his gentile state — if you say we should decree [that he must wait an eighth day], he would never bring a Paschal offering, and [the Sages] did not decree to that extent.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:7:1.hebrew: אבל ערל ישראל - שאם יש לו עכשיו טומאה, הוא נזהר בה, שאף בערילתו מקבל טומאה כשאר בני אדם; ליכא למיגזר ביה משום שנה הבאה:
Rashi on Pesachim 92a:7:1.english: But an uncircumcised Jew - For if he has ritual impurity now, he is careful about it, since even in his uncircumcised state he is susceptible to ritual impurity like other people; [therefore,] there is no [reason] to make a decree regarding him on account of next year.

Rashi on Pesachim 92a:9:1.english: An uncircumcised [person], sprinkling, and a scalpel - They are mnemonics for halakhic rulings.

Tosafot on Pesachim 92a:16:1.hebrew: ואמר רבי יוחנן דבר תורה אפילו עשה אין בו - ר' יוחנן לא פליג אברייתא, דלאו תנא הוא, כדמוכח בפ"ק דכתובות (דף ח.) גבי "אין אבלים מן המנין", דלא משני אר' יוחנן: "רבי יוחנן תנא הוא ופליג", כדמשני ארב; אלא פרושי מפרש לה. וכן מוכח, דגבי יולדת שהיא טבולת יום ארוך כתיב (ויקרא י״ב:ד׳): "ואל המקדש לא תבוא" — משמע: הא למחנה לויה תבא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 92a:16:1.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: By Torah law, there is not even a positive [mitzva] - Rabbi Yochanan does not disagree with the Baraita, for he is not a Tanna, as is proven in the first chapter of Ketubot (8a) regarding [the statement] "Mourners are not [counted] in the quorum," where [the Gemara] does not answer regarding Rabbi Yochanan, "Rabbi Yochanan is a Tanna and disagrees," as it answers regarding Rav; rather, he is explaining it. And this is also proven, for regarding a woman who has given birth, who is a tevulat yom arokh [one who has immersed and awaits her atonement], it is written (Leviticus 12:4): "And into the sanctuary she shall not enter" — which implies: but into the Levite camp she may enter.

Tosafot on Pesachim 92a:16:2.hebrew: טבול יום לא יכנס במחנה לויה - לא בכל המחנה, אלא מעזרת נשים ולפנים, כדתנן במסכת כלים (פ"א משנה ח): "עזרת נשים מקודש הימנו, שאין טבול יום נכנס לשם", אבל בהר הבית היה נכנס. וקרי חצר לעזרת נשים, כדתנן פ"ב דמדות: "עזרת נשים היתה אורך קל"ה, וארבעה לשכות היו בארבעה מקצעותיה של מ' אמה, ולא היו מקורות", וכן הם עתידות להיות, כדכתיב: "ויוציאני אל החצר החיצונה וגו'". וא"ת: מנא ליה דגזרו על טבול יום? דילמא על טמא מת גזרו, שהיה מותר בכל מחנה לויה! וי"ל: דטמא מת אפי' בחיל גזרו שלא יכנס, כדתנן במסכת כלים (שם): "החיל מקודש הימנה, שאין נכרים וטמאי מתים נכנסין לשם". והא דנקט בברייתא "וראה קרי בו ביום", ולא נקט "טבול יום" דשאר טמאים — רבותא נקט: לא מיבעיא שאר טמאים, דמדאורייתא מותרים ליכנס, אלא אפילו בעל קרי, דמשתלח מדאורייתא חוץ לשתי מחנות, אפ"ה טבול יום שלו לא גזרו ביה רבנן. ואם תאמר: דבפרק נוטל (סוטה דף כ:) פריך אהא דקתני התם "הוציאוה הוציאוה שלא תטמא את העזרה": "והתניא: טמא מת מותר ליכנס במחנה לויה, ואפילו מת עצמו כו'", ומאי פריך, כיון דמדרבנן אסור ליכנס? וי"ל: דמשמע ליה מדאורייתא, מדקאמר "הוציאוה הוציאוה" תרי זמני, שהיו ממהרין כל כך. א"נ: לא גזרו אלא שלא יכנס לפנים, אבל אם נטמא בפנים לא גזרו עליו לצאת. והא דאמרי' בהנשרפין (סנהדרין ד' פא:): "כהן ששימש בטומא' מוציאין אותו חוץ לעזרה ופוצעין את מוחו בגיזרין" — לאו דוקא חוץ לעזרה, אלא הוא הדין חוץ לחיל:
Tosafot on Pesachim 92a:16:2.english: One who has immersed on that day [tevul yom] may not enter the Levite camp - Not [meaning] the entire camp, but rather from the Women's Courtyard and inward, as we learned in a Mishnah in Tractate Kelim (1:8): "The Women's Courtyard is holier than it, in that a tevul yom may not enter there," whereas he was permitted to enter the Temple Mount. And [the verse] calls the Women's Courtyard a "courtyard" [chatzer], as we learned in a Mishnah in [chapter] 2 of Middot: "The Women's Courtyard was 135 [cubits] in length, and there were four chambers in its four corners, [each] of forty cubits, and they were not roofed," and so they are destined to be [in the future Temple], as it is written: "And He brought me out to the outer courtyard, etc." And if you ask: How does [the Gemara] know that they decreed against a tevul yom? Perhaps they decreed against one impure from a corpse [tamei met], who [by Torah law] was permitted throughout the entire Levite camp! One can answer: Against one impure from a corpse, they decreed that he may not enter even into the cheil [the rampart surrounding the Temple], as we learned in a Mishnah in Tractate Kelim (ibid.): "The cheil is holier than it, in that non-Jews and those impure from a corpse may not enter there." And as for why the Baraita stated "and he experienced a seminal emission on that day," and did not state "a tevul yom" of other impure persons — it stated a greater novelty: not only other impure persons, who by Torah law are permitted to enter [the Levite camp], but even one who experienced a seminal emission [ba'al keri], who is sent out by Torah law outside two camps, nevertheless the Rabbis did not issue a decree regarding his tevul yom status. And if you ask: In Perek [Hayah] Notel (Sotah 20b), [the Gemara] challenges what was taught there, "Take her out, take her out, lest she defile the Courtyard": "Was it not taught in a Baraita: One impure from a corpse is permitted to enter the Levite camp, and even a corpse itself, etc." — and why does [the Gemara] ask this, given that by rabbinic law he is forbidden to enter? One can answer: [The Gemara] understood [the Mishnah's statement] to be by Torah law, since it said "Take her out, take her out" twice, [indicating] that they were hurrying so much. Alternatively: They only decreed that he should not enter inside, but if he became impure while inside, they did not decree upon him to leave. And as for what we say in [Perek] Hanisrafin (Sanhedrin 81b), "A priest who served in a state of impurity — they take him outside the Courtyard and split his skull with clubs" — [that is] not specifically outside the Courtyard, rather the same law applies [that they take him] outside the cheil.

Tosafot on Pesachim 92a:3:1.hebrew: גבי פסח לא העמידו דבריהם במקום כרת - הא דלא קאמר משום דפסח מצוה עוברת, משום דיש קדשים דמצותן נמי עוברת, כגון תודה, דאין נאכלת אלא ליום ולילה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 92a:3:1.english: With regard to the Paschal lamb, they did not uphold their words in a situation of karet - The reason [the Gemara] does not say [that it is] because the Paschal lamb is a passing mitzvah [is] because there are [other] sacrifices whose mitzvah also passes, such as a thanksgiving offering, which is only eaten for a day and a night.

Tosafot on Pesachim 92a:7:1.hebrew: אבל ערל ישראל ד"ה טובל - תימה לריב"א, דלא מצינו בשום מקום טבילה בישראל שמל, אפילו מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Pesachim 92a:7:1.english: But [with regard to] an uncircumcised Jew, all agree [that] he immerses - It is astonishing to Riba, for we do not find anywhere [a requirement of] immersion for a Jew who was circumcised, even by rabbinic decree.
